pl-l4d1c9-d1e115.summary: Sets out to explain in whom circumcision was instituted, why, and why it was changed into baptism.

pl-l4d1c9-d1e118.summary: States that Abraham first received the command of circumcision, as a test of obedience; it was commanded not to him alone but to his seed, all the Hebrews, and was performed according to the Law on the eighth day, with a stone knife, on the foreskin.
claims: Circumcision was commanded to Abraham and his seed as a test of obedience.

pl-l4d1c9-d1e124.summary: Gives the reasons for circumcision: that Abraham might please God by obedience as Adam displeased him by transgression; as a sign of Abraham's great faith that he would have a son in whom all would be blessed; and to distinguish that people from other nations.
claims: Circumcision was given for obedience, as a sign of faith, and to distinguish the people.

pl-l4d1c9-d1e131.summary: Explains why it was performed on the foreskin: it was instituted as a remedy for original sin, drawn from parents through concupiscence, which rules most in that part; and since the first man felt the guilt of disobedience there, it was fitting that he receive the sign of obedience there.
claims: Circumcision on the foreskin answers original sin transmitted by concupiscence.

pl-l4d1c9-d1e134.summary: Explains the eighth day and stone knife: in the common resurrection, in the eighth age, all corruption will be cut away from the elect through Christ the rock; and by Christ's resurrection on the eighth day the soul of each believer is circumcised from sins. So there are two realities of that sacrament.
claims: The eighth day and the stone knife signify the resurrection and Christ.

pl-l4d1c9-d1e140.summary: Explains why circumcision was changed into baptism: baptism is more common and more perfect, with fuller grace. Circumcision only remitted sins, giving neither assisting grace nor the possession or increase of virtues, while baptism remits sins, confers assisting grace, and increases virtues; it is called water of refreshment. One already just by faith and charity receives fuller grace in baptism, but not so in circumcision: to Abraham, already justified by faith, it was only a seal and gave nothing inwardly.
claims: Baptism is more common and perfect than circumcision.
Circumcision only remitted sins; baptism also gives assisting grace and increases virtues.
Circumcision gave nothing inwardly to the already justified Abraham.

pl-l4d1c9.summary: Explains in whom circumcision was instituted, why, and why it was replaced by baptism. Abraham first received it, as a test of obedience, for himself and all Hebrews, performed on the eighth day with a stone knife on the foreskin. It was given so that Abraham might please God by obedience where Adam displeased by transgression, as a sign of his great faith, and to distinguish his people. It was performed on the foreskin because it was a remedy for original sin, drawn through concupiscence, which rules most in that part, where the first man felt his disobedience. The eighth day and the stone knife signify the general resurrection in the eighth age and Christ the rock. It was replaced by baptism, more common and perfect, which not only remits sins but confers assisting grace and increases virtues; circumcision gave nothing inwardly to Abraham, already justified by faith.
claims: Circumcision was given to Abraham and his seed as a test of obedience and sign of faith.
It was performed on the foreskin as a remedy for original sin transmitted through concupiscence.
The eighth day and stone knife signify the resurrection and Christ the rock.
Baptism replaced circumcision because it confers fuller grace.
Circumcision only remitted sin; baptism also confers grace and increases virtues.
